SNIC seeds & candidates — data-based thresholds

Burned vs unburned distributions of the period-based bpts metrics; commission/omission curves and a shallow tree to decide the seed/candidate cuts

Author

Iván Barberá

Published

July 6, 2026

Code 
library(data.table)
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(knitr)
library(rpart)
library(rpart.plot)

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 11))

# One row per training point, from scripts/bp_ts_metrics_local_train.R: the
# step-03 burn-probability time-series metrics recomputed locally over each
# point's OBSERVATION PERIOD (not a calendar year), using the deployed P050
# model on the fit-cleaned observations. label: 1 = burned, 0 = unburned.
# Period-based windows dissolve the cross-year + contamination problems (see
# docs/04-snic.md), so there is no negative-set gating here.
d <- fread("../data/annual_data_resolved.csv")
lab <- c(`0` = "unburned", `1` = "burned")

# Seeds (strict, K=3) vs candidates (loose, K=2): magnitude (pmaxK) + change
# (deltaK_peak) + persistence (minforeK_peak). docs/04-snic.md §"Tune seeds…".
seed_metrics <- c("pmax3", "delta3_peak", "minfore3_peak")
cand_metrics <- c("pmax2", "delta2_peak", "minfore2_peak")

1 What this notebook decides

Whether a simple empirical threshold / shallow tree on the recomputed bpts metrics separates burned from unburned points well enough to define the SNIC seed and candidate surfaces — or whether a second (annual) model is warranted (docs/04-snic.md §2). Rule of thumb: if a depth-2/3 tree on 3–4 metrics reaches near-ceiling separation (§4), the second model is unnecessary; a GEE random forest stays a fallback, not the plan.

Seeds and candidates have opposite objectives, so read every curve from two ends (§3):

  • Seeds → precision (few unburned above the cut). Seeds only need part of a scar; supervised SNIC grows the rest.
  • Candidates → recall (few burned below the cut). Candidates define the footprint SNIC may grow into; missed burned area is the real cost.

Validation. The local metric computation is checked against the exported bpts image on a single mid-year fire (scripts/test-bp_ts_metrics_local.R); run that before trusting the thresholds transfer to production (§7).

3 Per-metric distributions, burned vs unburned

Code 
long <- melt(d, id.vars = "label",
             measure.vars = c(seed_metrics, cand_metrics),
             variable.name = "metric", value.name = "value", na.rm = TRUE)

ggplot(long, aes(value, colour = factor(label, labels = lab))) +
  stat_ecdf(linewidth = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ metric, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(colour = NULL, x = "metric value (probability scale)", y = "ECDF") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
Code

       aes(factor(label, labels = lab), value, fill = factor(label, labels = lab))) +
  geom_violin(alpha = 0.6, scale = "width") +
  facet_wrap(~ metric, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL) +

4 Commission / omission vs threshold

For each metric, sweep the threshold: commission = fraction of kept points that are unburned (precision failure); omission = fraction of burned points below the cut (recall failure). Read the seed cut off commission, the candidate cut off omission.

Code 
co_curve <- function(dt, metric, n = 200) {
  v <- dt[[metric]]; y <- dt$label
  ok <- !is.na(v); v <- v[ok]; y <- y[ok]
  thr <- unique(quantile(v, probs = seq(0, 1, length.out = n), na.rm = TRUE))
  rbindlist(lapply(thr, function(t) data.table(
    metric = metric, threshold = t,
    commission = if (sum(v >= t)) mean(y[v >= t] == 0L) else NA_real_,
    omission   = mean(v[y == 1L] < t))))
}
curves <- rbindlist(lapply(c(seed_metrics, cand_metrics), co_curve, dt = d))

ggplot(melt(curves, id.vars = c("metric", "threshold"),
            variable.name = "error", value.name = "rate"),
       aes(threshold, rate, colour = error)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ metric, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent) +
  labs(x = "threshold (≥ kept)", y = "error rate", colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
Code

5 Joint separation & a shallow tree

Code 
ggplot(d, aes(delta3_peak, pmax3, colour = factor(label, labels = lab))) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.25, size = 0.6) +
  labs(colour = NULL, x = "delta3_peak", y = "pmax3") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
Warning: Removed 8519 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range
(`geom_point()`).
Code 
# Shallow tree as a GUIDE (not a deployable model): which splits does the data
# suggest, and does it plateau short of clean separation?
dt <- d[!is.na(delta3_peak)]
fit <- rpart(label ~ pmax3 + delta3_peak + minfore3_peak + pmax2 +
               delta2_peak + minfore2_peak + n,
             data = dt, method = "class",
             control = rpart.control(maxdepth = 3, cp = 0.005))
rpart.plot(fit, extra = 104, box.palette = "RdYlGn", nn = TRUE)
Code 
cat(sprintf("resubstitution accuracy (depth ≤3): %.3f\n",
            mean(predict(fit, type = "class") == dt$label)))
resubstitution accuracy (depth ≤3): 0.964
Code 
# Near-ceiling => empirical tree suffices, no second model. Clear plateau => model.

6 Stratification — does one threshold set hold?

Separability drifts by vegetation and observation density (grassland recovers fast, forest slow; sparse series overlap more). If the cut moves a lot across strata, seeds/candidates may need to be veg/region-stratified.

Code

  stat_ecdf(linewidth = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~ region, nrow = 1) +

7 Transfer to production & proposed thresholds

These metrics are period-based; production applies the cuts to the year-based bpts. Confirm the single-fire hard-check (scripts/test-bp_ts_metrics_local.R) passes on the magnitude metrics before committing thresholds. Then transcribe the seed (precision-side) and candidate (recall-side) cuts into config/snic_seed_candidate_thresholds.csv (hand-editable; the SNIC step reads them) and record here the values chosen, the reasoning, and whether a single global set held or stratification was needed.
